instruction: Export all open blog articles in Chrome as PDFs, using the blog post titles as filenames, and save them in /home/user/Documents/Blog.

metadata.explanation: Task requires downloading 2 blog articles as non-empty PDFs to /home/user/Documents/Blog, naming each file with the blog post title. Evaluator verifies: (1) at least 2 PDF files exist, (2) minimum size of 1000 bytes each (ensuring actual content), (3) filenames contain keywords from blog titles ('agent' for first post, 'human'/'data'/'quality' for second post). Custom getter retrieves file sizes and names, metric checks count, size, and filename requirements with partial credit.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Score is minimum of count_score and filename_score. Count_score: valid_files_count/min_count where valid files are >= 1000 bytes. Filename_score: matched_keywords/expected_keywords where filenames must contain keywords from blog titles.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete requirement coverage: Evaluator correctly verifies all 4 requirements - PDF format (by .pdf extension), correct location (/home/user/Documents/Blog), non-empty files (min_size_bytes=1000), and correct naming (expected_keywords matching)

Filename validation implemented: Metric checks if filenames contain expected keywords from blog titles - 'agent' for first post and 'human'/'data'/'quality' for second post (metrics/pdf_size.py:28-51)
Robust keyword matching logic: Case-insensitive matching with all keywords in a set required, handles blog title variations (spaces/dashes/case)
Proper partial credit: Score is minimum of count_score and filename_score, both requirements must be satisfied
Getter extracts correct state: get_pdf_file_sizes returns both file sizes and filenames needed for metric validation
Expected values are semantically correct: Keywords accurately represent blog titles from URLs (agent post, human-data-quality post)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor edge case: If one PDF filename contains keywords from both posts (e.g., 'agent-human-data-quality.pdf'), it could match both keyword sets. Consider adding uniqueness constraint to prevent one file from satisfying multiple keyword sets, though this is unlikely in practice.
